since Russell's set, Godel's sentences, anti-diagonal functions and consistency of Peano Arithmetic are not Diophantine then assuming PA is Diophantine consistent and Diophantine complete the set of Diophantine equations is decidable and turing complete (if it's solvable there is a proof and if it's unsolvable there is a refutation)

the set of register machines definable by {returnloop, inc r, dec r, jnz r l} is also decidable and turing complete, if you encode each instruction with a pair of natural numbers and each program as pairs of pair of natural numbers then each program end with a returnloop instruction and their semantics are as follows

0 0 if not the last instruction then go to the next line else if this program halt then return r1 else loop
r 0 increment register number r
0 r decrement register number r if not zero
r l go to line l if register number r is not zero
by compiling each program to a Diophantine equation you can solve the halting problem for this language, see here. the purpose of returnloop instruction is to prevent the construction of the anti-diagonal program.
